result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter is from Mr Osei, a bone and joint surgeon (orthopaedic surgeon). He wrote it to your GP. You got a copy.

It gives the results of a scan of your left knee. The scan was an MRI. An MRI is a scan that uses magnets to take detailed pictures inside the body.

The scan showed:
- There may be a small tear in the cushion inside your knee. It is in the back part of the inner cushion (posterior horn of the medial meniscus). This is only possible. A tear cannot be ruled out.
- There is no broken bone (fracture).
- A band inside your knee is not damaged. This is the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). The letter says it is intact.
- There is mild early wear and tear on the inner side of the knee (osteoarthritis).
- There is a little fluid in the knee.

Surgery is not planned at this stage.

## What you need to do
1. Mr Osei has sent you for physiotherapy for 6 to 8 weeks.
2. You can carry on with your normal activities as far as the pain allows.
3. Mr Osei will see you again in the bone and joint clinic (orthopaedic clinic) in 3 months.

The letter does not say who will book the physiotherapy. It does not say when it will start.

## Dates and medicines
- 1 September 2026: the MRI scan of your left knee was done.
- For 6 to 8 weeks: physiotherapy.
- In 3 months: you will see Mr Osei in the orthopaedic clinic. The letter does not give the exact date.

The letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What is physiotherapy, and who will book it?
- When will my physiotherapy start?
- What is the meniscus?
- How will I get the date for my clinic visit in 3 months?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
